claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 15 years old and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can help you assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to determine eligibility:

**Are you responsible for Alex? That is, do you provide for his care and upbringing (such as providing food, clothing, shelter, and looking after his day-to-day needs)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex - I provide everything for him. I make sure he has food, clothes, a place to live, and I look after all his day-to-day needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's an important factor.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** 

For example, is he studying for A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications at school or college?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He's just finished his GCSEs but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a follow-up question:

**Has Alex left education recently, and if so, when exactly did he finish his GCSEs?** I need to know the specific date or at least the month and year when his education ended.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He finished his GCSEs back in June - so about 6 months ago now. He left school at the end of the summer term.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the situation:

- Alex is 15 years old
- You are responsible for him (providing care, food, clothing, shelter, etc.)
- He finished his GCSEs in June (approximately 6 months ago)
- He is not currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training

Based on the Child Benefit rules, you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

**Child Benefit is generally payable for children under 16, or under 20 if they're in approved education or training.** Since Alex is 15 years old (under 16), you can claim Child Benefit for him regardless of whether he's in education or training.

Once Alex turns 16, the rules change - at that point, he would need to be in full-time non-advanced education or approved training for you to continue receiving Child Benefit for him. But until he reaches age 16, you qualify based on his age alone.
